essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Propose an approach to independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band on self-selected material and justify it before beginning.
Execute that approach independently, working at the high end of the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, independently and proficiently, documenting decisions as a scholar would.
Bound the resulting claim: state its limits, its strongest counter-case, and what would overturn it.
success_criteria: The learner states the method they chose and the known weakness of that method.
Every claim is traceable to a source the learner assessed for strengths and limitations relative to this task.
The learner reports what the evidence does not establish and what would overturn the claim.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

Ask the learner to attempt independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band cold, before any instruction. Record what they already do well. Nothing here is scored, and errors here are data, not failure.
Name what the diagnostic revealed in neutral, non-character language. State the unit question and what will count as evidence by the end of it.

Walk the unit's destination: Complete an independent close-reading dossier on a demanding text using a protocol the student designs.. The learner writes down what they think will be hardest about it and why. The tutor may question this prediction but may not write it.
The learner records one specific thing about independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band they intend to be able to do by the end of the unit.

student_activity: Attempt independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band without instruction, then record a personal goal for the unit.
formative_check: Name one thing about independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band you can already do and one you cannot do yet.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

adaptive_tutor_routes.action: Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band, re-teach it on a short passage, then retry one fresh item. Do not write the learner's response.
Ask the learner to explain why the move for independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.

Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require self-directed application on at least two separate occasions with no supplied method, including one piece defended against prepared objections from a reader outside the household when the family chooses.

mastery_rule: Do not mark mastery from one answer. Require self-directed application on at least two separate occasions with no supplied method, including one piece defended against prepared objections from a reader outside the household when the family chooses.
extension: Transfer the method to a different discipline or genre and account for what changes about evidence, audience, and convention.
student_authorship: The learner writes every assessed response. The tutor may explain, question, critique, or suggest a revision direction.
The tutor must not draft, rewrite, or supply sentences for an assessed response, and must not complete a graded task on the learner's behalf.
Tutor assistance is logged as guided evidence; unaided work is logged as independent evidence. Mastery requires independent evidence.
Fixed-form assessment items keep their answer key adult-only; the key is never surfaced in a learner-facing surface.
accessibility_and_accommodations: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and make the success criteria visible in text.
Allow typed, handwritten, dictated, or recorded-to-text responses; the response mode is not the standard.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, transcripts, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for any media.
Provide an accessible reading representation (digital reflowable text, enlarged print, or audio) for every assigned text.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
safety_and_privacy: Use respectful, non-shaming language about writing and reading difficulty.
Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Offer an alternate text or private response when content is personally sensitive.
Do not require autobiographical disclosure; fictionalized or analytical alternatives are always acceptable.
Presentation may be delivered privately to the facilitator; no public or recorded performance is ever required.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, annotated passage, recorded reading, or short clip supporting independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable text, alt text, or a transcript. No media is required to meet the standard.

home_connection: Invite the learner to notice one real-world instance of independence at the high end of the 11-CCR band in something they already read. No purchase, account creation, or private disclosure is required.

essential_question: How does close, evidence-governed attention to self-monitoring and repairing comprehension change what a reader or writer is entitled to claim?
learning_objectives: Propose an approach to self-monitoring and repairing comprehension on self-selected material and justify it before beginning.
Execute that approach independently, working at the high end of the grades 11-CCR text complexity band, independently and proficiently, documenting decisions as a scholar would.
Bound the resulting claim: state its limits, its strongest counter-case, and what would overturn it.
success_criteria: The learner states the method they chose and the known weakness of that method.
Every claim is traceable to a source the learner assessed for strengths and limitations relative to this task.
The learner reports what the evidence does not establish and what would overturn the claim.
materials: course notebook or digital equivalent
the unit's assigned texts, in an accessible reading representation
citation reference or style manual appropriate to the course

lesson_flow.teacher_or_tutor_action: Open with a short retrieval prompt on self-monitoring and repairing comprehension. Ask the learner to predict, recall, or pose a question before any instruction.

No worked exemplar is supplied. The facilitator states the standard and the audience, then asks the learner to propose an approach and justify it before beginning. Keep the explanation centered on self-monitoring and repairing comprehension.

The learner designs the approach, names its known weakness, and revises the plan after a single round of critique. The facilitator questions and critiques but does not supply the method. The object of practice is self-monitoring and repairing comprehension.

The learner executes their own method on self-selected material, documents decisions as a scholar would, and reports the limits of the resulting claim. The learner writes this response; the tutor may question or critique but may not draft it.
In one concise response, state the most important claim about self-monitoring and repairing comprehension and one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.

formative_check: State the most important claim about self-monitoring and repairing comprehension and identify one check that would expose a weak or unsupported reading.
answer_or_scoring_guidance: Score the stated learning target, accuracy, evidence and reasoning, and revision. Accept multiple valid readings when the evidence supports them. Do not infer effort, motivation, diagnosis, or character from an error.

Ask the learner to explain why the move for self-monitoring and repairing comprehension works on this text before continuing. Accept explanation in any modality.
Name specifically what the reasoning got right about self-monitoring and repairing comprehension, offer one varied case, and avoid unnecessary remediation.
Describe the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a correct case, and schedule a short later review of self-monitoring and repairing comprehension.
Decline to supply the assessed response. Offer a question, a criterion, or a counterexample instead, and record that guided support was given.
